page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and Intel Xeon 8559C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical dedicated cores running at 3.2 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz. It includes advanced hardware instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix operations, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions.

A primary architectural feature of the i7ie.xlarge is its bundled local storage, offering 2500 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity. The instance includes 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without an attached discrete GPU accelerator. Memory density is high at 8.0 GB per core, backed by an extensive cache hierarchy featuring 320 MB of shared L3 cache.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread performance, with Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 10 percent and single-threaded gzip compression exceeding 34 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput on workloads such as software compilation with Clang and stress-ng multi-core testing reflects the physical limitation of its 2 physical cores. Memory read bandwidth uncached large blocks registered at 34.18 GB/sec, while in-memory operations reached 6.09 million Redis SET operations per second.

The hardware configuration provides high storage and memory density relative to compute allocation, making it cost-efficient for workloads bound by I/O and RAM rather than raw compute scaling. The i7ie.xlarge is well positioned for transactional databases, distributed storage nodes, caching layers, and search index operations requiring low-latency NVMe access.
